what: Ahzi-Tal, a Helstrom courier, lodges for one night. Reeh-Shaal, who pays for her bed in salt and travels the same road, sees that his satchel holds a sealed packet his ledger does not list.
Reeh-Shaal buys a length of rope from Tsono-Ra after the lodge has closed, saying she needs it to tie her pack.

Reeh-Shaal kills Ahzi-Tal at the stone lip, takes the satchel, ties the body's wrists and pins it with a grave-stake in the spring's throat under the Hist's roots, so it will not float up. She leaves the stake's face uncarved.
Haj-Tei finds the courier's bed empty, his pack still in the lodge store and his bill unpaid. He decides the courier left before dawn without paying and keeps the pack against the debt.
The body fouls the water. Guests who drink it, or eat food cooked in it, fall sick with fever and retching.
Reeh-Shaal stays at the lodge, saying she waits for a boat to Helstrom. She waits for the packet's buyer, who has not come, and tells the sick guests it is the fire stand's food.
After the lamps are out, Reeh-Shaal goes to the stone lip and looks down into the water for a while, to be sure the body has not come up.

In a dry year the founders went down the root galleries and cut a channel from a brine seam toward the roots of a rival grove downstream, to sour its water and take its travellers. The rival grove withered; Greenspring grew.
The founders carved the descent on their own grave-stakes in the old way, as a deed done for the tribe, and never spoke of it to outsiders.
With the grove downstream dead, the channel silted on that side; each flood now pushes the brine back up the cut into Greenspring's own taproots.
Vees-Wai finds the Hist's leaves falling out of season and the sap thin. The village tastes salt in the spring and blames the salt works upstream.
Ixo-Vaal stopped trading for salt-works salt when the works closed their landing; he now buys upriver rock salt, which he keeps in a sack at his door.
